summary: The exact candidate implements and mock-tests one server-wide fixed LoRA adapter for all DSpark draft requests. It does not implement the original per-task choice of draft adapter/model and collapses distinct task adapter identities at the draft forward boundary. The narrower path is partially verified, but real DSpark adapter execution is unavailable in this environment.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: collection fails because the base has no sglang.srt.speculative.dspark_lora module or DSpark draft LoRA support.
Candidate regression suite: 10 tests passed, covering mocked fixed-manager creation/routing, empty-path rejection, and existing DSpark defaults.
Independent original-contract counterexample: expected two distinct per-task draft adapter IDs; observed the same server-wide fixed adapter ID for both rows.
Three existing GPU tests passed for LoRA TARGET_VERIFY eager/CUDA-graph metadata on the assigned gfx950 GPU; this is supporting infrastructure evidence, not end-to-end DSpark proof.

gpu_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 and HIP 7.2.26015. GPU tensor execution and three TARGET_VERIFY LoRA metadata tests passed.
remaining_counterexamples: Two tasks cannot select distinct DSpark draft adapters: both draft rows are forcibly assigned self.draft_model_runner.dspark_lora_id.
There is no request-level DSpark draft-adapter field or propagation separate from target-model lora_id/lora_path.
There is no multi-adapter DSpark draft registry, dynamic load/unload path, scheduler admission/draining policy, or mixed-adapter batch lifecycle.
The alternative of multiple draft models for one target model is not implemented.
remaining_limitations: No compatible DSpark base checkpoint and stage-2 LoRA adapter were available, so end-to-end output numerics and acceptance-rate improvement were not measured.
DSpark CUDA-graph capture/replay with real adapter weights remains unverified; mocked routing and generic LoRA metadata tests do not establish it.
The tiny Llama fixture cannot qualify DSpark architecture or adapter semantics and was not used as substitute evidence.
No native source changed, so native rebuilding was not applicable.
Only one assigned AMD gfx950 GPU was used; distributed and other architecture paths were not tested.
